audit.whatIsWrong: phases[0..4].side all read "Skill" while win[0..3] read Swain and win[4] reads Anivia — five rows where the page answers itself twice, including the level 6 flip.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock sustain and a 3-second-at-rank-5 Death's Hand hold the lane through level 5; Glacial Storm at 6 is the flip, and the packet chart agrees with the content layer on every row.

Anivia's ladder is right. Swain's spike is Demonic Ascension at a flat 120s, and the form lasts indefinitely as long as he keeps draining champions — so denying him a body is what ends it, not waiting out a duration.
audit.corrected: Wrote the 120s and the drain-dependency into the cooldown and trading lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer puts Swain's root on W twice ("Root you with W", "root you with W then drain you down with Q and E"). His root is Nevermove (E); W is Vision of Empire, a long-range eye that damages, slows and reveals. Nothing anywhere states the interaction that decides the lane: Nevermove only roots on the way BACK.
audit.why: Riot's text: "Swain launches a wave of demonic power forward. It then returns to Swain and roots enemies it hits. Swain can then choose to pull all rooted champions closer." A player dodging the outgoing wave and then standing still is exactly who gets rooted and pulled into Demonic Ascension's 650-range drain.
audit.corrected: Fixed the slot names and wrote the return-hit rule into the cooldowns, trading and don'ts.
sources: brief enemyKit E and W Riot text

audit.why: Nevermove is 12s at rank 1, Vision of Empire 22s, Death's Hand 7s falling to 3s, Demonic Ascension a flat 120s. None appeared anywhere in the matchup.
audit.corrected: All four written into breakdown.cooldowns and the phase whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Itemization mentions anti-heal only as a trailing clause and never says when.
audit.why: Ravenous Flock heals him and permanently raises his max health, and it is flagged percentHealth — so stacking raw resistances is the wrong answer and Grievous Wounds timing decides every extended trade.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal timing tied to his first big item in breakdown.feeding rather than left as a footnote.

edits.after: Survive the early range war, then out-clear and out-zone him with storm and wall. Every commit starts with one question: is Nevermove down its 12 seconds?

edits.before: Swain wins by landing Demonic Ascension, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Swain wins by rooting you on Nevermove's return, pulling you into a 650-range drain, and healing back everything you spent.

edits.before: Threaten Q until Swain burns his sidestep tool, land it, then E + auto and walk before the answer — chilled E double-damage is the whole trade.
edits.after: Trade in the 12 seconds Nevermove is down: Flash Frost first, then Frostbite for the doubled chill damage, and leave before Death's Hand stacks bolts.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Swain walks straight at you.
edits.after: Standing still after you dodge Nevermove — the wave roots on its return trip, and the pull that follows puts you inside his drain range.

edits.before: - Swain Demonic Ascension: matchup-defining — His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget W Crystallize for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Nevermove: 12s at rank 1, 850 range, and it roots on the RETURN — keep moving after the dodge. - Death's Hand: 7s down to 3s, more damage per bolt. - Vision of Empire: 22s. - Demonic Ascension: 120s, 650 range, and it lasts while he drains.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by denying the pull: he needs Nevermove's return to land before anything else works, so hold Crystallize on his walk-up line and never fight inside 650.

edits.before: If Swain takes first blood, tighten up: Demonic Ascension is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with R wave-clear and stay relevant through zone control.
edits.after: If Swain takes first blood, buy Grievous Wounds with your first big item — Ravenous Flock heals him back through chip and grows his max health permanently. Two kills: farm with R wave-clear and stay outside 850 units.

edits.before: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Swain away from the comeback farm, and rotate first to every river fight with your stun loaded.
edits.after: Ahead, the lane is a prison: storm every wave, wall Swain off the comeback farm, and step up on the 12 seconds Nevermove is down — he has no other way to hold you.

edits.before: Q-E online — a landed stun now means a real chunk. Trade only when his engage tool is down; your mana hates wasted rotations.
edits.after: Q-E online — a landed stun means a real chunk. Trade with Nevermove on its 12 seconds; Ravenous Flock heals back anything you leave unfinished.

edits.before: Hit Lost Chapter timing and the mana war ends. Chip Swain with max-range Q threats and bank Manaflow stacks.
edits.after: Lost Chapter ends the mana war, but chip alone does nothing here — Ravenous Flock converts it back into permanent health. Poke to force a recall, not a kill.

edits.before: His drain mode — disengage and reset the fight when it starts. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Demonic Ascension lasts as long as he drains a champion — walk out of the 650 range and it simply ends.

edits.before: That’s Swain’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Ravenous Flock turns your chip into permanent max health — poke without a kill threat feeds him.

edits.before: Swain's Q-W-E DoT chain and free sustain from Ravenous Flock let him win extended trades and out-poke your egg cooldown before level 6.
edits.after: Death's Hand stacking bolts and free sustain from Ravenous Flock win him every extended trade, and Nevermove's return root sets up the kill before level 6.

edits.before: Rylai's slow uptime on Storm and Flash Frost lets you kite his short root range and burst him down before he can drain-tank the fight.
edits.after: Rylai's slow uptime lets you hold the 850 units Nevermove needs, and Grievous Wounds is what stops him drain-tanking the fight through your burst.

edits.before: His root-into-drain combo keeps punishing your lack of mobility through level 3.
edits.after: Nevermove's return root into the pull punishes an immobile bird through level 3.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 remain his since Demonic Ascension is close and he can force any extended fight in his favor.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay his: Death's Hand is down to 4 seconds and his sustain wins anything extended.

edits.after: Save Wall for his walk-up — he needs 850 units for Nevermove

notes: Slot error corrected: the content layer put Swain's root on W twice, but W is Vision of Empire (long-range eye, slow and reveal, 22s) and the root is Nevermove (E). The decisive mechanic — Nevermove roots on its RETURN trip, then pulls — was absent everywhere and is now the spine of the matchup. Both packet suspectNames entries are false positives: "Use Demonic Ascension" and "Glacial Storm's" are both correctly spelled, the second being Anivia's own R in a possessive. content.early still contains the same "root you with W" slot error inside a long paragraph; I left the paragraph rather than rewrite 400 characters, so it needs a follow-up pass.
